ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in circle $\odot O$, CD is a tangent with the point of tangency at D, and line CO intersects $\odot O$ at B and A, where $\angle A = 35^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $\angle C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Connect OD, \\
$\because$ CD is the tangent line of $\odot$O, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ODC = $90^\circ$, \\
Also $\because$ $\angle$COD = 2$\angle$A = $70^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$C = $90^\circ - 70^\circ = \boxed{20^\circ}$

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a circle with center O, with A, O, B, C lying on one straight horizontal line, D on the lower-right part of the circle, chord AD drawn, and CD tangent at D. From the text, use that CD is tangent at D and that line CO passes through the center, so AB is a diameter; the marked angle at A is ∠DAB = 35°. Draw radius OD. Since a radius to a tangent point is perpendicular to the tangent, ∠ODC = 90°. The inscribed angle ∠DAB intercepts arc DB, so the central angle ∠DOB is 2 × 35° = 70°. Because C, O, B are collinear, ∠COD = ∠BOD = 70°. In right triangle COD, ∠C = 90° − 70° = 20°.
